claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me the name(s) of the child or children you're inquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm inquiring about my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm glad to help you with Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to gather some details about your circumstances. Let me start with the first question:

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 16 years old. He was born in early 2008.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to understand your residency status to determine eligibility.

**What is your residency status in the UK? Are you a British citizen, settled status holder, or do you have another type of visa or residency arrangement?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen and I live here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful information.

Now I need to ask about Alex's current situation:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training, or is he working?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he actually just left school recently. He's in that period where he's signed up with the careers service to figure out what he wants to do next - you know, getting advice about his options for college or work or whatever.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining Alex's situation. That's useful context.

I need to clarify a bit more about his current status:

**Has Alex started any full-time education, apprenticeship, or approved training since leaving school, or is he currently only receiving careers guidance without being enrolled in any formal education or training programme?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't started anything formal yet. He's just registered with the careers service at the moment, getting guidance while he figures out his next steps.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification.

I have one more important question to help determine eligibility:

**Is Alex receiving any other benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not getting any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me make sure I have the full picture before I provide my assessment.

**Are there any other children you're inquiring about for Child Benefit, or is Alex the only child you're claiming for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, it's just Alex I'm asking about.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the key details:
- Alex is 16 years old (born early 2008)
- You are a British citizen residing in the UK
- Alex has recently left school and is currently registered with the careers service receiving guidance, but is not enrolled in any formal full-time education, apprenticeship, or approved training
- Alex is not receiving any benefits in his own name

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, I need to inform you that **Alex would not be eligible for Child Benefit** at this time.

Here's why: Child Benefit for young people aged 16-19 continues only if they are in full-time education or approved training. Since Alex has left school and is currently only receiving careers guidance without being enrolled in any formal education or training programme, he does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

However, this situation could change if Alex enrolls in full-time education, an apprenticeship, or other approved training - at which point you could potentially claim Child Benefit again.
